usdRate.sourceName: Sveriges Riksbank, SEK per USD (SWEA series SEKUSDPMI)

inflation_cpi.sourceName: Trading Economics, Sweden inflation rate (SCB CPI, secondary source)
inflation_cpi.note: CPI up 1.1% year on year in September 2026 (0.3% in August); CPIF, the Riksbank target measure, 1.5%. SCB's own site could not be reached. Eurostat HICP for Sweden: 1.0%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: Riksbank inflation target (2% CPIF); CPI 1.1% in September 2026
inflation_projection.note: The Riksbank targets 2% CPIF inflation and has kept inflation near target outside the 2022-23 spike, so 2% is used for planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: Sveriges Riksbank, policy rate (SWEA series SECBREPOEFF)

savings_account_rate.note: No typical savings-account rate could be read. Statistics Sweden (SCB), which publishes bank interest rates on household deposits for the Riksbank, could not be reached (connection refused on scb.se and api.scb.se).

fdr_3m_rate.note: No typical 3-month fixed-term deposit (fasträntekonto) rate could be read. Statistics Sweden (SCB), which publishes bank interest rates on household deposits for the Riksbank, could not be reached (connection refused on scb.se and api.scb.se).

fdr_1y_rate.note: No typical 1-year fixed-term deposit (fasträntekonto) rate could be read. Statistics Sweden (SCB), which publishes bank interest rates on household deposits for the Riksbank, could not be reached (connection refused on scb.se and api.scb.se).

dps_rate.note: Swedish banks do not sell a standard monthly recurring deposit product with a published rate; regular saving goes into ordinary savings accounts or an investment savings account (ISK).

bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: World Bank FR.INR.DPST for Sweden stops in 2006. Statistics Sweden (SCB), which publishes bank interest rates on household deposits for the Riksbank, could not be reached (connection refused on scb.se and api.scb.se).

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No retail government savings certificate or savings bond is sold to individuals in Sweden today; the Debt Office (Riksgälden) ended its retail savings products, and government securities are bought through banks on the market.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Sveriges Riksbank, Swedish Treasury bill 3 months (SWEA series SETB3MBENCH)

tbond_5y_rate.sourceName: Sveriges Riksbank, Swedish government bond 5 years (SWEA series SEGVB5YC)

tbond_10y_rate.sourceName: Sveriges Riksbank, Swedish government bond 10 years (SWEA series SEGVB10YC)

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Sweden taxes on personal income
tax_bank_interest.note: Capital income, including bank interest, is taxed at a flat 30%; banks report interest to the tax agency rather than withholding a final tax. Savings inside an investment savings account (ISK) are taxed instead by a yearly standard levy.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No retail government savings certificate exists; interest on government securities is ordinary capital income taxed at 30%.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: Riksgälden (Swedish National Debt Office), how the deposit insurance works
deposit_insurance_limit.note: SEK 1,150,000 per person per institution (changed from SEK 1,050,000 in 2025); up to SEK 5 million extra for deposits from specified life events such as a home sale.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: Sweden caps interest on high-cost credit (reference rate plus 40 percentage points) but no readable official page confirming a cap or typical rate for credit cards could be reached (Konsumentverket page moved).

equity_return_low.sourceName: OMX Stockholm 30 at 3,271 on 30 Oct 2026, +18% over the year (Trading Economics)
equity_return_low.note: Low case: after the 2025-26 rally Swedish shares return only a little more than safe bills.

equity_return_base.sourceName: OMX Stockholm 30 (Trading Economics); 3-month Treasury bill 2.10% less 30% tax = 1.47%
equity_return_base.note: Base set at the after-tax bill rate plus about 4 points, the cap; the Stockholm index has a strong 10-year record, so the full premium is used.

equity_return_high.sourceName: OMX Stockholm 30 long-run record; long-run global equity returns
equity_return_high.note: High case: diversified Swedish and global equity funds matching their long-run record of about 8% in kronor.

gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps pace after the 2025-26 spike, and a firmer krona trims returns.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); Riksbank 2% inflation target
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises with world inflation plus a little, with the krona assumed stable against the dollar.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend in krona terms.

fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax, below the policy rate.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 3-month Treasury bill 2.10% less 30% capital income tax = 1.47% (Riksbank SETB3MBENCH)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: the after-tax Treasury bill rate, a proxy for fixed-term deposits.

fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: holding longer government bonds after tax.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Finansinspektionen does not publish an industry-wide life insurance claim settlement ratio that could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover (livförsäkring/risklivförsäkring) is sold, often through employers and unions, but no regulator or official premium table per SEK 1,000 of cover was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: Hospital care is provided by the regions with a small daily inpatient fee and a yearly high-cost cap; the 1177 regional fee pages could not be read, and no figure for a private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Private health insurance (sjukvårdsförsäkring) is mostly an employer benefit priced per person, not per SEK 100,000 of cover; no published premium table was found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Eurostat HICP Sweden, health (ECOICOP 2 CP06): -5.9% year on year in September 2026
goal_inflation_health.note: The recent fall reflects policy changes to patient and medicine fees; over the long run health costs are planned at 3%, a point above the 2% target.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Eurostat HICP Sweden, education (CP10): -15.2% year on year in September 2026
goal_inflation_education.note: Schooling and university are free for residents and the measured index is volatile; the fees people do pay (courses, private pre-school, materials) are planned at 3%.

life_expectancy.sourceName: Eurostat, life expectancy by age and sex (demo_mlexpec), Sweden
life_expectancy.note: Men 82.3, women 85.3 in 2024; World Bank 2024 total 84.06.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: Eurostat, life expectancy by age and sex (demo_mlexpec), Sweden 2024

support_ratio.sourceName: Eurostat EUROPOP2023 projections, old-age dependency ratio (proj_23ndbi, baseline)
support_ratio.note: 100 divided by the projected old-age dependency ratio (65+ per 100 aged 15-64): 33.2 in 2026, 36.9 in 2040, 44.8 in 2065. World Bank 2025: 33.5.

retirement_age_default.note: Riktålder (target pension age) is 67 for people born 1960-1966 and projected at 68 for those born 1970-1981, 69 for 1982-1997 and 70 for 1998-2014; earliest public pension withdrawal 64-65 for the 1970s cohorts. Same for men and women.

retirement_age_government.note: Swedish public employees follow the same public pension ages and employment-protection rules as private employees; no separate statutory retirement age for government service could be confirmed from a readable official source.

retirement_return_low.note: Low case: easy-access savings after tax.

retirement_return_base.note: Base case kept just under the after-tax Treasury bill rate.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: a ladder of longer government bonds after tax, a little under the 10-year yield.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if shares lag.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half shares at 5.4% and half safe fixed income at about 1.5-2% after tax.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning balanced mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Maximum guarantee pension SEK 11,988 a month before tax for a single person and SEK 10,853 for a married person in 2026, for 40 years' residence; it is reduced as income-based pension rises.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Paid from the riktålder (67 from 2026, rising with life expectancy for later cohorts); needs at least 3 years' residence, full amount after 40 years from age 16. Not means-tested on assets, but reduced against the person's own income-based pension.

gratuity_rule.note: Swedish law (LAS) sets notice periods but no statutory gratuity or severance per year of service could be confirmed from a readable official source; severance (avgångsvederlag) comes only from collective agreements.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Pensionsmyndigheten, the Swedish pension system and riktålder
public_pension_scheme.note: Allmän pension: 16% of pensionable income to the notional income pension and 2.5% to the funded premium pension (18.5% in all). Pension from the riktålder, projected at 68 for people born 1970-81 (earliest 65). Pensions in payment follow wage growth less 1.6% rather than prices; taxed as income.

dps.note: No standard recurring-deposit product; regular saving goes into savings accounts or an investment savings account (ISK).

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No retail government savings certificate or bond is sold directly to individuals.

tbill_91d.note: Traded in large lots, mainly by institutions; individuals reach them through funds.

equity_fund.note: Widely available, often held in an investment savings account (ISK) taxed by a yearly standard levy; the state default premium-pension fund is a global equity fund.

gold.note: Investment gold is exempt from VAT and freely bought.

insuranceComplaints.name: Allmänna reklamationsnämnden (National Board for Consumer Disputes)
